summary: The search query is fully parameterised, the sort fragment comes from a fixed allow-list, and the offset is clamped. I found nothing that needs fixing before release.

The audit leaves out the payment-verification check, even though the repository has tests/release/test_payment_verification.py and other audits mark that check as critical. The release evidence is incomplete, so GO cannot be recorded until the check is run and passes at commit 43a2f97.

GET /projects trusts the client-supplied x-org-id header and never checks it against res.locals.user.orgIds. Any logged-in user can list another organisation's projects and budgets (IDOR / tenant isolation break).

RLS is enabled with owner-scoped select, insert, update and delete policies. The update USING clause also acts as the check, and anon is revoked, so saveNote cannot change other users' notes. I found nothing blocking.

Confirmed medium finding AG-007: login has no per-account rate limit. It is formally accepted with an owner, an approver, edge IP rate limiting as a compensating control, and a two-week fix date, and all other critical checks pass at the release commit. Release on condition that the per-account limit ships as committed and that the NOT APPLICABLE status on ai-permissions is confirmed.

DELETE /api/internal/users/[id] only calls requireSession and sits outside the /api/admin middleware matcher. Any authenticated member can permanently delete any user account. The admin suspend route also relies only on the middleware, with no role check of its own.

The webhook verifies the Stripe signature, grants the plan only when payment_status is paid (including async success), and makes the event-id deduplication atomic with the account update inside a transaction. I found nothing blocking.

Checkout offers delayed payment methods (bacs_debit, customer_balance), but the webhook grants 'pro' on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status and ignores async_payment_succeeded/failed, so users get the plan before paying. Deduplication is also a non-atomic check-then-insert that records the event before processing, so a concurrent delivery races and a failed update is never retried.

The URL allow-list is a plain string prefix check, so hosts like https://images.partner-cdn.com.attacker.net or https://images.partner-cdn.com@evil pass. The server also follows redirects, which allows SSRF to internal or metadata endpoints. Parse the URL, compare the exact origin, and disable or re-validate redirects; also limit size and content type.

Confirmed high finding AG-004: password reset tokens never expire (a two-day-old token was accepted). It is accepted only on the grounds that reset volume is low, with no compensating control. This account-takeover risk should be fixed before release rather than accepted.

The critical ownership check was run against the older commit 7fd543e, not the release commit 43a2f97, and src/routes.py (the ownership query) changed in between. The ownership evidence is stale, so the check must be re-run at the release commit before GO.

document_preview is SECURITY DEFINER, so it bypasses RLS, and it does not filter on owner_id = auth.uid(). Any authenticated user can read the title and first 280 characters of any document by ID. Add the owner filter or make the function SECURITY INVOKER.

The critical ownership, tenant-isolation and payment-verification checks are recorded as PASS, but their commands are 'true' or 'echo tenant isolation verified', so they never ran the tests. That evidence is fabricated and does not support GO.

transfer() accepts any Decimal amount, including negative values (and NaN or Infinity), so a negative amount passes the funds check and moves money from the recipient to the sender. Validate that the amount is finite, positive and properly quantised. Also handle a missing or invalid recipient (currently a 500 error) and lock rows in a consistent order to avoid deadlocks.

The critical tenant-isolation check is marked PASS on static review only, with no command or exit code. Its claim of organisation scoping does not match the code, which filters by owner_id. A critical check needs runtime evidence at the release commit before GO.

The invoice route requires a session and reads through a Prisma extension that forces userId on findFirst and findMany, and it returns only non-sensitive fields. I found no blocking issue, but note that other invoice operations (findUnique, update, delete) are not scoped if someone uses them later.

`...input` is spread after the server-side product fields, so a client can send unitAmount (and name) in each item and override the price, for example paying 1p for any product. Build line items only from server data plus a validated integer quantity and a length-limited note.
